content.title: Your Crop Rotation Report
content.summary: Your current maize and soybean rotation scores 67.1. The fill the bare gap option with cereal rye cover crops scores highest at 78.5. It keeps the soil covered all year and builds soil better. The save water option with canola instead of maize scores 67.7 and needs about 73 mm less water stress a year than now. The break the pest cycle option with sunflower scores lowest at 66.8 and needs about 64 mm more water stress a year than now. These numbers come from NASA data and your goals to build soil.
content.what_satellites_see: From space this spot looks like 100% cropland. Your field usually looks bare or newly planted from October to April. The soil where roots drink is driest in September and wettest in May. About 840 mm of rain falls a year, with very little in January and more in June. Heat of 35 °C or more is common in July and August. Frost is likely from October to May.
content.bare_and_risky_seasons: Your current rotation leaves the field bare for eight months: January through May and October through December. These are the same months when frost is likely. July and August are the hot months while your crops grow.
